# WO-2026-08-14-02 — the bananas gap

**Small order. One behaviour. Warwick has told this build twice today that it is not enterprise software —
build it plainly.**

## The finding, by execution on live

`POST /api/asdair/check-item {"text":"bananas"}` returns **`unmatched_new_item`** — even though the
household has `ASDA 6 Bananas`, now carrying `display_name = "Bananas"`.

**Why: the matcher reads `name` and `aka` only — which is correct and must stay that way. But the 55
products that needed a `display_name` are exactly the ones with NO `aka` at all.** So for over half the
catalogue the duplicate nudge can never fire. `"milk"` worked only because it happened to already be an
alias on the Cravendale.

## Warwick's ruling — the boundary, verbatim

> *"the new sense-check may compare Mum's typed text against display names for duplicate detection, but it
> must never feed `display_name` into catalogue resolution or mutate matching behaviour. If a display-name
> check is ambiguous, do not choose a product and do not expose candidate lists to Mum."*

## Acceptance criteria

**AC1 — a display-name duplicate check, in `checkItem.js` only.**
Before or after the resolver — your judgement — compare her text against `display_name` using the
**normalisation the estate already has** (`normaliseTerm` from `resolveByCatalogue.js`, imported read-only)
rather than a new one. **Exact normalised equality only. No fuzzy matching, no substring, no scoring.**
On a hit, answer `status: "matched"` with that row's `display_name` and `id`.

**AC2 — ⛔ the resolver is not touched, and `display_name` never reaches it.**
`resolveByCatalogue.js` is **outside your surface and must not change.** `display_name` must not be passed
into `resolveReading`, must not enter the regulars objects handed to it, and must not alter any existing
result. **WP-B15-51's AC5 test already pins this — show it still passes.**

**AC3 — ambiguity refuses, and refuses silently.**
If two active regulars share a normalised `display_name`, **return `needs_confirmation` with
`matched_name: null` and no candidate list.** Warwick's words, and this build's standing rule: **Mum is
never asked a question.**

**AC4 — the resolver still wins where it has an answer.**
A term the catalogue resolves confidently must keep resolving to the same `matched_regular_id` as today.
**Prove `"milk"` still returns id 4.** This check adds reach; it must not redirect anything.

## Required evidence

- `cd services/asdair/cockpit-api && node --test` → real counts. **Baseline 422 / 422 / 0 / 0** with the
  disposable target set. `interpret` (36/36) must be unmoved — it is the matcher's own suite.
- **The live behaviour, before and after, against the real 109 rows:** `bananas`, `milk`, `richmond`,
  `deodorant`, and one term you expect to be ambiguous.
- `bash scripts/secret-scan.sh --surface services/asdair/cockpit-api/checkItem.js services/asdair/cockpit-api/checkItem.test.js` → exit code and coverage.

## Explicitly out of scope

- `resolveByCatalogue.js`, `loadCatalogue.js`, anything under `interpret/`.
- The UI. Felix renders whatever `matched_name` you return, in parallel under WP-B15-52.
- Seeding or editing any `display_name` value.

## Sequencing

**READ-BACK AND HOLD — short is fine.** Then build, commit on
`build-015/b15-53-display-name-dupcheck` in `C:/Fusion247PKA-dupcheck`, and push. No PR, no merge, never
`main`.

**Do not build defence-in-depth around this.** One comparison, one test per AC. The last package was
simplified mid-build because I over-specified it; do not make me do that twice.
